posts.title: A Clear Membership Journey
posts.text:
A Clear Membership Journey

FTI presents a practical sequence for understanding the ecosystem: discover its components, explore the applications and review the details before deciding on an action.

Membership, the reserve-based token and governance each have a distinct role. Start with the member workspace when your purpose is to review an account or understand participation.

There is no need to complete every action in one session. Familiarity with the interface gives each later confirmation a clearer context. The pinned introduction provides the main platform links.

posts.title: Your Workspace, in Context
posts.text:
Your Workspace, in Context

The member workspace brings account information into a single interface. Its membership view, wallet details and activity sections serve different purposes, so begin with the overview before selecting a specific action.

Review the account you have connected, then consider the information associated with that address. Membership position and progression belong to the account being displayed, rather than to the browser itself.

Use navigation to move deliberately between sections. A clear starting point makes it easier to distinguish account information from an operation that requires wallet approval.

posts.title: Begin with the Correct Account
posts.visual_subtitle: Match the address to your intent.
posts.text:
Begin with the Correct Account

An account review begins with a simple detail: the public address currently connected to the application.

If your wallet manages more than one address, confirm that the selected account is the one you intend to use. Then compare it with the address displayed in the member workspace before interpreting membership details or continuing to an action.

A different connected address represents a different account context. Taking a moment to establish that context helps keep your registration, account review and later wallet confirmations aligned.

posts.title: A Network Check Before an Action
posts.text:
A Network Check Before an Action

The network selected in a wallet is part of an operation's context. Check it alongside the network shown by the FTI application before proceeding.

The configured FTI deployment uses BNB Smart Chain mainnet, chain ID 56. Confirm that your wallet and the application refer to the same network when reviewing account information or preparing a transaction.

An address alone does not describe every part of that context. Network, account and intended action should be considered together before a wallet confirmation is approved.

posts.title: Keep the Referral Context Clear
posts.text:
Keep the Referral Context Clear

A referral link establishes the starting context for a membership registration. When one has been provided, use that link to enter the application and review the sponsor information presented during the process.

Compare the complete address with the information you received, rather than relying on a shortened label or familiar opening characters. Address accuracy matters before confirmation.

Keep the original link available while reviewing the registration. It provides a useful reference if the displayed sponsor needs clarification or the entry process requires assistance.

posts.title: Understand Each Confirmation
posts.text:
Understand Each Confirmation

Wallet connection, token approval and a contract action have different roles. A connection allows the interface to use your public address; it does not by itself authorize spending.

When the application requests a further confirmation, review what that particular request is asking you to approve. Consider the account, network and operation shown, rather than treating every wallet prompt as the same step.

A deliberate sequence keeps the process understandable: establish the account context, review the application details and assess each requested authorization on its own terms.

posts.title: Read Your Membership View
posts.text:
Read Your Membership View

The membership area is the place to review your participation and network context. The overview also presents membership progression and account information associated with the connected wallet.

Read these elements together. A rank label, progression indicator or purchased-unit figure describes a particular part of the account; no single field explains every aspect of participation.

When moving from review to management, confirm that the account remains the one you intend to use. The workspace is designed to help you inspect the relevant information before choosing the next action.

posts.title: Inside the Binary Network
posts.text:
Inside the Binary Network

FTI membership includes a binary network structure. The network view provides a visual starting point for understanding how the displayed positions relate to the connected account.

Look at the structure alongside your membership information and activity, rather than reading the diagram as an earnings forecast. A network position and a token balance represent different records.

Open the member workspace, choose the network section and explore the available account details. Save this guide as a reference when explaining the platform's structure to another participant.

posts.title: Give Account Data Its Context
posts.text:
Give Account Data Its Context

An account screen communicates more than numbers. Loading indicators, request notices and information freshness help explain what is currently available to review.

Allow the relevant data request to finish before drawing conclusions from a view. If the application shows previously retrieved activity information, read the accompanying notice so you understand its context.

For an operation already submitted to the network, the transaction hash and confirmed receipt provide a separate reference. Account presentation and transaction confirmation answer different questions, and both deserve careful attention.

posts.title: The FTI Visual Signature
posts.text:
The FTI Visual Signature

The metallic mint three-ribbon emblem is the visual signature used on the FTI website and in this official channel. The glass series carries that same original mark into each educational card.

Look for a consistent identity across the website, member workspace and token application, then use the published official links to reach the page you need. A logo is a useful visual reference; the destination address remains the direct way to identify a link.

Share the original channel posts when introducing the ecosystem so the artwork, context and platform links travel together.

posts.title: A Quote Is a Snapshot
posts.text:
A Quote Is a Snapshot

FTI’s internal quote reflects the active contract’s reserve and supply mechanics. It should be read alongside the current transaction conditions, rather than treated as an external market valuation.

Other transactions can change contract state before your operation confirms. Fees, execution limits and the amount requested also affect the result.

Review the current quote in the token application and check the minimum output before making a decision. Reserve accounting does not guarantee profit or repayment.

posts.title: Verify the Deployment
posts.text:
Verify the Deployment

A familiar token name is only the beginning of verification. The network and full contract address identify the deployment you are reviewing.

In the token application, find the deployment information and follow its explorer link. Compare the complete address, then inspect the available contract and transaction records. A copied screenshot or shortened address is insufficient for this check.

Before authorizing an operation, confirm that the wallet request matches the network, contract and action you intended. Begin with the official token application.

posts.title: Read Transaction Status Carefully
posts.text:
Read Transaction Status Carefully

Submitting a transaction, receiving confirmation and refreshing application data are separate events. A balance refresh problem does not, by itself, establish that a confirmed transaction failed.

If a status remains unclear, retain the transaction hash and inspect the receipt through your wallet or the network explorer before considering another submission. Check any freshness notice when reviewing activity history.

Use the member application to review the information available, and compare it with the confirmed on-chain record. This helps prevent decisions based on an incomplete screen update.

posts.title: Review the Complete Quote
posts.text:
Review the Complete Quote

The amount entered is one part of a token operation. Review the estimated output or net proceeds, applicable fees and minimum accepted amount together.

A displayed spot price does not replace the quote for your chosen transaction size. If the quote is unavailable, refresh the contract data and resolve the issue before proceeding.

In the wallet, review the requested action and network fee as well. Open the token application to inspect the current conditions for the operation you are considering.

posts.title: Understand Spending Permissions
posts.text:
Understand Spending Permissions

A token approval authorizes a specified contract to spend an allowed amount. Review the token, spender address and allowance before confirming that request. Approval and the subsequent purchase remain separate actions.

Disconnecting a wallet session does not necessarily remove an on-chain approval. If you choose to revoke an allowance, follow your wallet’s documented controls and review the resulting network transaction. Revocation does not reverse completed transactions.

Return to the official application to check the intended operation before granting any new permission.

posts.title: Read Beyond the Introduction
posts.text:
Read Beyond the Introduction

The FTI whitepaper provides a structured introduction to membership, token mechanics, fees, settlement and governance. Use it to understand how the components relate before reviewing an individual operation.

Read the relevant section in context, then compare it with the active application’s deployment details and current quote. An explanation of a mechanism is not a personal earnings estimate.

Open the official presentation, note the sections relevant to your questions and keep a copy for reference. The page also supports printing or saving as PDF.

posts.title: Follow the Roadmap with Context
posts.text:
Follow the Roadmap with Context

The official roadmap describes current capabilities and the checks that remain ahead. Read each stage together with its stated scope, rather than assuming that every described capability is already available.

For an operation you intend to use, review the current application and its deployment information. A roadmap provides development context; the active contract and confirmed transaction determine execution.

Visit the roadmap to understand the sequence of work and use official channel announcements as a starting point for reviewing published updates.

posts.title: Membership and Tokens: Separate Records
posts.text:
Membership and Tokens: Separate Records

Membership units and an FTI token balance describe different parts of the ecosystem. The member dashboard is the place to review registration, units and network information. The token application presents token balances, reserves and transaction quotes.

Read the label attached to each value and choose the application that matches your question. An approval request also deserves its own review: check which contract is requesting permission and which operation follows.

Start from the official website to open the relevant workspace and explore its supporting documentation.

posts.title: Prepare a Clear Support Report
posts.text:
Prepare a Clear Support Report

A precise report helps technical support understand what happened. Include the page, intended action, exact error message, device, browser and approximate time. For a submitted transaction, retain its hash and describe the status shown.

If you attach a screenshot, remove confidential information first. Never include a wallet recovery phrase or private key. State what you observed without assuming the cause.

Check the official website’s contact details before sending your report. The listed support address is Support@FTIProtocol.com. Keep your original notes for any follow-up.

https://ftiprotocol.com/
